b: Your list starts full, not empty. Make a trip and you get a packing list already built from a library of 863 items across 36 ready-made lists, with kits you add as you need them.
Your job is deleting, not writing. Crossing things out is easy. Staring at a blank list is not. The whole app is built around that difference.
A trip has five phases — Prep, Pack, Travel, Plans, Return — so "packing" stops being one enormous task and becomes five small ones that arrive when they're relevant.
Nothing you do in a trip changes your library, and nothing in your library changes a trip you've already made. You can experiment freely.
It all lives on your phone. No account, no sign-in, nothing to set up.

t: Pack for a weekend trip in five minutes
b: Tap "+ New Trip". Type where you're going. The emoji picks itself.

t: Pack for a weekend trip in five minutes
b: Set the dates and tap the pills that describe the trip — how you're travelling, what the weather's doing. About thirty seconds of tapping.

t: Pack for a weekend trip in five minutes
b: Tap Next, glance at the pre-ticked lists, tap Go Pack. Don't agonise here; you can add and remove anything later.

t: Pack for a weekend trip in five minutes
b: You now have a full packing list. Work down it. Delete what you don't need as you go.

t: Pack for a weekend trip in five minutes
b: Everything after this point is refinement. The trip already exists and nothing is fragile.
Drop whole lists first. Tap Manage Sections (top right), then the red − beside anything you don't need. One tap can remove twenty items.
Then swipe individual items left to delete. No confirmation, no ceremony.
Collapse everything you're not doing right now. Tap a group's row to fold it shut.
Filter down to one kind of thing when the mix is the problem — ••• → Filter → Items to Pack.
None of this touches your library. Delete as recklessly as you like; next trip starts fresh.
Tap the + circle at the bottom right. A search field opens at the top of what you're looking at. Type. Press return. Done.
The field stays open after each item, so you can dump five things in a row without tapping anything again.
It searches your library as you type — pick a match and you get its notes, quantity rules and charging info for free.
No match? Tap Create "…" and it's added as a one-off for this trip.
Drag the + instead of tapping it to drop the new item at an exact spot in the list.
Tap the circle to check something off. It shows as done for about a second, then gets out of your way.
Your phone won't lock while you're on a packing list. Put it down, cross the room, come back.
Some items appear twice on purpose — checking one checks the other. The eyebrow "Also in …" tells you when.
Swipe left to delete, swipe right to flag as critical (or the reverse — it's a setting).
Press and hold any row for everything else: quantity, edit, critical, charged, delete.

t: Travel day and the Double Check
b: The Travel tab ends with a Double Check panel — right at the bottom, below everything else. You don't have to build it, find it, or turn it on.

t: Travel day and the Double Check
b: It gathers every Critical item from your Prep and Pack lists into one short list.

t: Travel day and the Double Check
b: Ticking it there is a separate confirmation from packing it. Packed means "it's in the bag"; double-checked means "I have looked at it with my own eyes."

t: Travel day and the Double Check
b: It's last on purpose. You work the list top to bottom, and this is the final gate before the door — so it's the last thing you meet.

t: Travel day and the Double Check
b: Above it sit On You and Departure Sequence — what's in your pockets, and the last sweep of the house.
You pack twice, so the app resets twice. Your Pack and Travel lists can be wiped clean and run again for the journey home.
The app offers this itself the first time you open the trip on or after the day before you come back.
House tasks stay ticked. "Run the dishwasher" doesn't come back. "Phone charger" does.
The tab bar quietly changes the day after you arrive: Prep steps aside, Return appears.
You can reset as many times as you like — a five-hotel trip resets five times.
••• → Save as Template turns the trip you just refined into a reusable starting point.
Best moment to do it: the day you get home, when you know exactly what you over-packed.
Heart a template to pin it to the Home screen's template menu — new trip in two taps.
Or skip templates entirely: Past Trips → Copy as New Trip clones a trip you've already taken, exactly as you left it.
Templates keep your sections, items, quantities and notes. They never keep dates, destination, or what you'd ticked off.
A trip has five phases — Prep, Pack, Travel, Plans, Return — because "packing" isn't one job.
A phase holds sections (Clothes, Toiletries), a section holds groups (Tops, Shoes), a group holds items.
The tab bar shows four phases at a time. Prep and Return trade places once you're home.
Your library is the cookbook. A trip is the meal. Editing the cookbook never changes a meal you've already cooked.
Kits are sections that don't share. Two kits can each hold sunscreen, and they're two bottles.
A template is a whole trip setup, minus the dates. Sections, items, quantities, notes, tags.
Three ways to make one: save a trip you've finished, save a past trip, or build one from scratch.
Heart your favourites and they appear in Home's template menu — a new trip in two taps.
Templates feed new trips only. Editing one never changes a trip you've already made.
Templates don't cover the Plans phase. Everything else comes across.
Settings → Sections & Kits Library holds 21 ready-made lists. Browse Kits offers 15 more you can add — 36 in all.
A section files things; a kit is a bag you grab. Two kits can each own sunscreen. Two sections share one licence.
Priority decides what you're offered: Essential (pre-ticked), Favorite (offered high), No Priority (offered when relevant).
Tags decide when a section is relevant — trip type, weather, season, transport, length.
Archive instead of deleting. Archived lists stop being offered but can come back.
Settings → Item Library is the master list of every item the app knows about.
An item carries its own rules: how many, which sections it belongs to, whether it's critical, whether it needs charging, when it's relevant.
Edits here reach the next trip you make, not the one you're packing.
One item can live in several sections — that's what makes "Also in Travel Documents" work.
Archive rather than delete. Deleting is permanent; archiving is not, and neither one harms an existing trip.
An item can work out its own quantity from your trip's length. Six rules to choose from.
Underwear and socks are "Days + 2". Shirts are "Days ÷ 2". That's most of what the library uses them for.
The number is worked out when the trip is created — and then it's yours to override.
Change your dates later and the per-day numbers recount — the app asks first, and never touches a number you set by hand.
Set formulas in the Item Library. On a trip you just set a number.
Outfits live on the Plans tab, not on the packing list. Nothing to turn on — the block is there on every trip.
Tap Add Outfit, name it, add garments, Confirm. Cancel writes nothing at all.
Each garment lands on your packing list under its TYPE — Tops, Bottoms, Shoes — because that's how a closet is arranged.
Naming a garment decrements the generic count it replaces. Plan a navy T-shirt and "T-shirt ×3" becomes "T-shirt ×2" plus your navy one. Your total stays right.
Underwear and socks never decrement. A specific pair you planned is an extra, not a swap.
One garment, one row. Wear the same shirt three days and it's one line reading worn 3 times.
Plans is for the trip itself, not for packing: what you're doing, what you're wearing, and things you want to remember.
Three blocks: Outfits, Activities, and Notes to Self.
Nothing here counts. Ticking things on Plans never affects a packing count or trip progress. It's yours.
Day pills let you look at one day at a time, or all of them at once.
There's no Manage Sections here — add sections with the Add Section row at the bottom.
Completed trips move to Past Trips and become read-only.
"Copy as New Trip" is the fastest way to plan again — you get last time's list exactly as you left it.
You have three days to change your mind. After that a completed trip's dates lock.
Search, filter and sort by type, weather, transport, season, length or name.
Getting there: the View Past Trips button at the bottom of the Home screen.
Settings is the gear at the top left of Home.
Libraries is the important part — templates, sections and kits, items.
Actions holds three behaviour switches, one of which only affects trips you haven't made yet.
Appearance does font, text size and light/dark.
Reset Options is destructive and lives behind its own screen.
Two screens, and the second one is optional. Welcome, then "What do you pack?" That's it.
There's nothing to sign up for. No account, no email, no password.
The second screen trims your library so you're not scrolling past things you'd never take.
Skipping is safe. It keeps both clothing sets and adds nothing — the same as leaving it alone.
Nothing is permanent. Everything you turn off is recoverable later.
Most "bugs" here are the app being deliberate — checked items hide, library edits don't reach old trips, and a planned garment quietly lowers the generic count it stands in for.
A few are genuinely misleading, and they're marked below as such.
There is no undo anywhere. Worth knowing before you delete something.
Section files things; kit is a bag you grab whole. Sections share items, kits don't.
Group is the collapsible row inside a section (Tops, Shoes).
Critical means "would ruin the trip", and feeds the Double Check.
Library means "the definitions", not "your trips".
Archive is reversible. Delete is not.
